subject: Post-call recap: VPC residency, air-gapped constraints, and decision asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@hearthcare.io>, security@hearthcare.io
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: VPC residency, air-gapped constraints, and decision asks

Maya / Security team — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and actionable asks so we have a shared decision path. Please reply with clarifications or confirm items below.

Key pain & goals (as we heard):
- Data residency requirement: all PHI telemetry and inference logs must remain in your AWS account in us-west-2; no Redwood-hosted logs may contain raw PHI.
- Network isolation: prefer carrier-grade air-gap model with outbound-only egress via customer-managed NAT/gateway; no inbound SSH from our control plane.
- Auditability: retention of request/response audit trail for 365 days, with KMS-managed keys.
- Deployment model preference: Private (customer VPC) but open to Dedicated if isolation guarantees can be matched.

Open technical constraints you mentioned
- The VPC must not accept incoming connections on non-standard ports; we need to verify which ports (you mentioned 443 only).
- Any sidecar/agent must be permitted to write to your S3 bucket with specific prefix and IAM role (SC-related).
- On-prem air-gapped site: limited egress window (daily 30-minute sync) and physical HSM requirement for key custody.

Immediate asks / next steps (please assign owners):
1) Maya: confirm whether KMS is customer-managed HSM (Y/N) or AWS KMS is acceptable, and any certs/accounts we need.
2) Security team: share minimal required egress endpoints/ports (CIDR or FQDN list) and the outbound sync window if on-prem is required.
3) Karthik/Redwood: we'll attach a lightweight network sketch and a security-question matrix for you to drop answers into; expect concrete failure modes and fallback behaviors in a follow-up.

Attachments: hearthcare_vpc-sketch.pdf (sketch), hearthcare_security_questions.xlsx (matrix).

Proposed timeline:
- Clarify security requirements and confirm KMS by 2028-06-06.
- Redwood to deliver an integration plan and initial SOW estimate by 2028-06-13.

If this looks right, reply with confirmations and who should be on the procurement thread.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

---
P.S. Monica: flagging for pricing sketch and whether Dedicated pool needs to be quoted separately for air-gapped cadence.
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@hearthcare.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@hearthcare.io, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 15:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VPC residency, air-gapped constraints, and decision asks

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) KMS/key management: our security team requires HSM-backed keys; we operate AWS CloudHSM and will need the integration to use a customer-managed key.
2) Ports & egress: primary outbound must be to our proxy on 443; we allow outbound DNS and HTTP(S) only. If Redwood needs to pull packages, pulls must be routed through our proxy.
3) On-prem sync window: for the air-gapped install at our Salt Lake City site, we have a 20-minute outbound sync once per day (02:00-02:20 UTC).
4) Logging: we cannot accept any raw inference outputs in your logs if they contain PHI; we will accept hashed identifiers and redacted traces.

I've looped in security@hearthcare.io for more granular answers and a small questionnaire they'll fill in — they should return the answers by EOD Friday 2028-06-02.

I'll also need a short note for procurement about whether Redwood requires install access or if you can operate under our-managed gateway model.

— Maya
Director, IT Operations | HearthCare
maya.singh@hearthcare.io

Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VPC residency, air-gapped constraints, and decision asks

Appreciate the fast reply, Maya — that helps a lot. Short follow-up and where Redwood will take action: 

What Redwood will do (by 2028-06-13):
- Provide a Customer VPC integration guide that supports CloudHSM and VPC-only egress via customer proxy.
- Draft an operational runbook for the Salt Lake City air-gapped install that respects the 20-minute daily sync window; outline failure/retry behavior and backpressure handling.
- Produce a redaction strategy for logs (hashing strategy & deterministic salt) and a sample audit pipeline showing 365d retention using customer-managed keys.

Questions we still need from you:
- Security: the exact CIDR/FQDN list for allowed outbound. If you're unable to provide CIDRs, an allow-list of FQDNs and proxy exception headers will suffice.
- Procurement: confirm whether we should assume Redwood will need temporary ops accounts for the initial install (we can design a least-privilege, time-limited role), or if you will manage the gateway for all pulls/pushes.

Attached: hearthcare_vpc-sketch.pdf (network sketch) and hearthcare_security_questions.xlsx — please have your security team drop answers into the matrix.

If these actions look correct I'll schedule a technical deep-dive with our CloudHSM engineer and our on-prem install lead for next week. Proposed windows: Thu 2028-06-07 or Fri 2028-06-08 (US morning).

Best,
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: procurement & commercial note (HEARTHCARE)

Quick internal note — capture here so we can brief pricing and procurement: 
- Risk/complexity: CloudHSM + 20-min daily sync + no raw PHI leaves us leaning toward Private deployment (customer VPC) with a separate air-gapped SOW for Salt Lake site.
- Pricing ask: Ben, please prepare a two-option quote: (A) Private VPC (multi-region failover) with KMS integration; (B) Private + on-prem airgap SOW (one-time install + annual support).
- Contract asks: add explicit audit-read access window and SLAs for daily sync window observability.

I'll coordinate the technical deep-dive invites once we have security's filled matrix.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
